title: Privacy Policy
description: How the current static website handles information.

sections.title: About this website
sections.text: Simpyll is a personal portfolio and educational publication. For privacy questions or requests, contact simpyll.com@gmail.com. This policy describes the website practices identified in the October 2026 source audit; hosting-provider settings and retention details have not been independently verified.

sections.title: Hosting and connection information
sections.text: GitHub Pages is configured to serve this website. Delivering pages involves connection information such as IP address, requested URL, browser information and request time. GitHub may process technical information under its own privacy statement. Provider log access, retention and deletion settings have not been independently verified; Simpyll does not promise a retention period for them.

sections.title: Cookies and browser storage
sections.text: Optional Google Analytics 4 is disabled until owner activation and visitor opt-in on this page. Before opt-in no Google analytics script loads. If enabled and allowed, Google processes canonical page paths and engagement using analytics cookies (configured lifetime 90 days); queries, fragments, page titles and referrers are excluded from manual page views. Google receives connection information. Advertising consent remains denied. The simpyll-analytics-consent preference is stored locally until changed or cleared. Withdraw on this page to stop collection and remove accessible GA cookies; already processed data is not automatically deleted. It stores an explicit theme choice in localStorage under simpyll-theme, until changed or cleared through browser settings. Session storage under simpyll-scroll-v1 holds up to 100 navigation entries, including paths, queries, fragments and scroll positions, to restore reading position. Session storage normally lasts for the tab session; browser session restoration can extend it. These values are read in your browser and are not sent to an application backend by this code. Blocking storage leaves fallback behavior available.

sections.title: Public aggregate reporting
sections.text: Pulse may publish daily site-wide Search Console and GA4 aggregates through authenticated publishing jobs. No raw search queries, visitor identifiers, IP addresses, demographic segments or per-visitor records are exported. Missing data is not zero. Daily public snapshots retain up to 730 days; repository history and public copies can persist longer. Detailed page-level breakdowns are omitted pending privacy review. Google account retention is separately configured by the owner; for requests contact simpyll.com@gmail.com.

sections.title: Search and third parties
sections.text: Search downloads a same-origin search-index.json and matches queries in the browser. No query submission endpoint was found. Fonts are bundled locally. Social buttons are external links. Approved YouTube embeds load only after you choose to activate each one; YouTube may then collect connection and browser information under its own practices. Following an external link sends you to a separate service with its own practices. Article media may use external image URLs; loading those images can disclose connection information to their hosts. Notion publishing and GitHub Actions run during publishing, not as visitor-facing APIs.

sections.title: Messages, retention and choices
sections.text: There is no on-site contact form, newsletter signup or comments system in the inspected implementation. Public GitHub reports disclose your account and submitted text to GitHub, maintainers and other readers. Repository history and public copies can persist after edits; no deletion timetable is promised. Do not post private requests, credentials or patient information. Clear site storage in your browser to remove local preferences and saved positions. GitHub controls requests concerning its own processing under its privacy statement.

sections.title: Privacy requests and international visitors
sections.text: For privacy questions or requests, email simpyll.com@gmail.com rather than posting sensitive information in a public GitHub issue. Describe your request and the information concerned; identity verification and response handling will depend on the request and applicable law. Depending on your location and applicable law, rights may include access, correction, deletion or objection. This policy does not claim that every jurisdiction's rules apply. Third-party processing may occur outside your country; provider arrangements and retention practices have not been independently verified.

sections.title: Children and future changes
sections.text: The portfolio and professional education focus is not designed as a service for children; no child-specific submission feature was found. The intended audience needs owner confirmation. New forms, analytics, embeds, AI services or clinical tools require a fresh privacy and consent review before launch. Analytics is optional and requires affirmative consent on this page. Owner activation remains contingent on reviewing applicable privacy duties, Google processing terms, retention and intended audience.

sections.title: Policy updates
sections.text: Changes will be reflected on this page and in source history. For questions about changes, email simpyll.com@gmail.com. No email notification system exists.

title: Terms of Use
description: Conditions for using this personal publication.

sections.title: Use of the website
sections.text: These terms describe use of Simpyll as a personal portfolio and educational publication. They are published by the site operator for informational use; no claim is made that an attorney reviewed them.

sections.title: Permitted use
sections.text: Read, link to and discuss the site responsibly, subject to applicable law and any specific permissions. Do not disrupt availability, misuse contribution channels, submit malicious material or disclose confidential information. Healthcare material is general education, not individualized professional advice.

sections.title: Content and software rights
sections.text: Public visibility is not an unrestricted reuse license. Consult an explicit license for each repository or asset before reuse; absent one, do not assume permission beyond applicable law. Code, articles, images and third-party materials may have different rights. Licensing and attribution decisions remain open under issue #88; these terms do not select a license or override third-party rights.

sections.title: Accuracy, availability and external services
sections.text: Learning notes and experimental software can contain errors or become outdated. Independently check information before relying on it. Availability, completeness and fitness for a particular purpose are not promised. External services operate under their own terms. This draft does not exclude rights or responsibilities that applicable law does not allow to be excluded; liability language requires qualified review.

sections.title: Changes and contact
sections.text: Substantive changes are recorded in source history. Public factual or technical corrections can use the page-specific GitHub link. For private legal or policy questions, email simpyll.com@gmail.com. No governing-law, arbitration or indemnification provision has been selected.

title: Medical & Educational Disclaimers
description: Boundaries for healthcare education and experimental tools.

sections.title: General education
sections.text: Healthcare and nursing content is for general educational and informational purposes. It is not individualized medical advice, diagnosis or treatment. Reading or interacting with this website does not establish a clinician–patient relationship.

sections.title: Independent clinical judgment
sections.text: Do not substitute this material for independent clinical judgment, institutional protocols, professional standards or consultation with an appropriately qualified professional. Evaluate publication dates, references and subsequent updates: healthcare knowledge and guidance change.

sections.title: Emergencies
sections.text: Simpyll is not an emergency service and does not provide urgent individualized guidance. For an emergency, contact your local emergency service or seek immediate in-person care; do not wait for a website response.

sections.title: Protect patient privacy
sections.text: Do not submit identifiable patient information in GitHub issues, edits or any other contribution channel. Do not reproduce identifiable clinical cases without appropriate authorization and safeguards. Removing a name alone may not prevent identification.

sections.title: Experimental tools and regulatory boundaries
sections.text: Future clinical calculators, assessment tools and educational software need feature-specific validation, limitations, source and licensing checks, and appropriate legal review before release. No clinical validation, professional accreditation, HIPAA certification, HIPAA compliance, FDA clearance or medical-device approval is asserted here. A disclaimer does not eliminate legal or professional responsibilities.

sections.title: Report an inaccuracy
sections.text: Use the page-specific correction link for non-sensitive clinical or technical errors, including the public URL and supporting reference. Never put patient details in a report. For private questions, email simpyll.com@gmail.com. Healthcare liability and applicable legal language may require qualified review.

title: Editorial Standards & AI Disclosure
description: Research, learning in public, AI assistance and corrections.

sections.title: Mission and scope
sections.text: Simpyll documents practical engineering, technology, healthcare perspectives and learning in public. Personal experience and experiments should be distinguished from established evidence. These standards describe editorial goals, not a claim that every existing article underwent a formal review.

sections.title: Research and verification
sections.text: Sources should support the claim, favor original documentation and primary research where practical, and be checked for currency and context. References allow readers to investigate further. No formal peer review or independent clinical review is claimed. Existing articles may differ in sourcing depth; report unsupported or outdated claims.

sections.title: AI assistance
sections.text: AI tools may assist with brainstorming, organizing research, drafting, editing, coding, debugging and testing. AI output can be incorrect or omit context. Assistance is distinct from independent human verification, source checking and executable tests. No blanket claim is made that every statement or code change has been personally verified. No visitor-facing AI service was found in the inspected application.

sections.title: Corrections and contributions
sections.text: Use the contextual GitHub link below each page to suggest a correction. Report factual errors, broken links, outdated guidance, clinical inaccuracies or software defects with the public page URL and evidence. Some article links open a correction issue because Notion is their editorial source; accepted corrections must be applied there before synchronization. Public reports require a GitHub account. Review and response times are not guaranteed; private feedback is available at simpyll.com@gmail.com.

sections.title: Publication and updates
sections.text: Article publication dates identify original publication and should not be treated as a clinical review date. Substantive corrections should be explained and distinguished from original publication. Meaningful updates use explicit editorial dates; optional revision histories and correction notices disclose changes separately from original publication. Automated synchronization and deployments do not change editorial dates. Policy drafts carry a separate review date; Git history records source changes.

sections.title: Material interests
sections.text: No sponsorship or affiliate arrangement was established by the website source audit, which cannot verify off-site relationships. Material connections, if present or introduced, should be disclosed beside the relevant content or links. Questions about potential conflicts can be sent to simpyll.com@gmail.com.

title: Accessibility Statement
description: Accessibility goals, tested scope and remaining limitations.

sections.title: Goal and approach
sections.text: Simpyll targets WCAG 2.2 Level AA through semantic structure, keyboard navigation, visible focus, readable contrast, responsive layouts and reduced-motion support. Automated tests do not establish complete conformance; no full conformance claim is made.

sections.title: Documented testing
sections.text: The repository accessibility record documents axe checks, keyboard and route navigation, theme behavior, text-spacing and reflow automation on Linux. Recorded CI run 40135762399 passed its browser gate with 476 passes and six existing isolated-fixture skips; separate fixture gates passed. It installed Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, with desktop and Pixel 7 Chromium contexts. Engine installation alone is not evidence that every scenario ran in each engine. This historical result does not certify subsequent changes.

sections.title: Known limitations
sections.text: Manual NVDA, VoiceOver and TalkBack testing, physical-device touch and virtual-keyboard checks, actual 200%/400% browser zoom and human visual/motion review were not documented as completed when issue #43 was closed. Mobile emulation and text enlargement are not equivalent to real-device or assistive-technology validation. See the accessibility audit for known limitations.

sections.title: Feedback and follow-up
sections.text: For accessibility problems, email simpyll.com@gmail.com or use the page-specific GitHub contribution link for non-sensitive reports. Include the affected URL, browser, device, assistive technology if applicable, and the blocked task. Do not submit personal health information. No response deadline or full WCAG conformance claim is made.
